reading.body:
Flexential Jacksonville publishes 1.39 MW of IT capacity across 35,184 square feet of technical space. At 10 kW per rack, a common enterprise colocation density, that load supports roughly 139 racks; at 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, it supports roughly 35 racks. The arithmetic is 1,390 kW divided by the assumed rack draw. The operator has not published a per-rack power envelope, so neither figure is the operator's claim.

The seven certifications qualify this campus to host regulated workloads: SOC 1 Type 2 and SOC 2 Type 2 attest to audited controls over financial and operational reporting; PCI DSS qualifies it for payment card data; HIPAA and HITRUST qualify it for protected health information; ISO 27001 certifies an information security management system; SSAE 18 is the attestation standard underlying the SOC reports. Which tenants use which certifications is not published.

Florida has 13 facilities mapped in this site's dataset, of which only 3 publish a megawatt figure, totaling 7.54 MW. Flexential Jacksonville contributes 1.39 MW of that total and ranks third among the three facilities with published capacity. At 1.39 MW it is a small facility by any measure relevant to AI scaling, where meaningful training clusters begin in the tens of megawatts. It is not a candidate for frontier model training infrastructure at its published size, though it could support inference endpoints or regulated AI applications tied to healthcare or payments.
